scope: Additional safe classroom experiment concepts only.

experiments.title: Ice melting observation 2
experiments.focus: Show again that a solid can change into a liquid without becoming a new substance.
student_observations: The ice shrinks over time.
Liquid water appears around the ice.
The change is physical, not a new substance.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful as a second review activity after the first phase-change lesson.

experiments.title: Water freezing review
experiments.focus: Introduce the idea that cooling can turn liquid water back into solid ice.
student_observations: Liquid water can become a solid again.
Temperature affects state changes.
The substance can stay the same while the state changes.
experiments.teacher_note: Pairs well with melting to show reversibility in a classroom model.

experiments.title: Water evaporation observation
experiments.focus: Show that liquid water can slowly disappear into the air as vapor in a model situation.
student_observations: The water level can go down over time.
Nothing new needs to be added to explain the change.
Heat and airflow can matter in evaporation ideas.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep it conceptual and compare with drying puddles.

experiments.title: Soap and water surface tension 2
experiments.focus: Show that a small amount of soap can change how water behaves at the surface.
student_observations: Bubbles may form more easily.
The surface behaves differently.
Some changes are physical and not chemical.
experiments.teacher_note: Good for a short demo before discussing mixtures.

experiments.title: Salt water evaporation 2
experiments.focus: Show that when water leaves a solution, the dissolved solid can remain behind.
student_observations: The solution becomes less liquid over time.
A solid residue can remain.
Evaporation can separate some mixtures.
experiments.teacher_note: Connect the idea to drying, salt pans and crystallization.

experiments.title: Sugar vs salt dissolving 2
experiments.focus: Compare how two familiar solids behave in water.
student_observations: Both solids can dissolve in water in the model.
Different substances can dissolve differently.
Clear solutions are not all identical.
experiments.teacher_note: A good review activity after introducing solutions.

experiments.title: Oil and water layers
experiments.focus: Show that some liquids do not mix evenly and can form layers.
student_observations: The liquids can separate into layers.
Not every liquid mixes with water.
Density and miscibility are useful ideas.
experiments.teacher_note: Use this to introduce immiscible liquids in simple language.

experiments.title: Sand in water mixture
experiments.focus: Show that some solids stay visible in water instead of forming a clear solution.
student_observations: The water can stay cloudy.
Particles may remain visible.
This is a mixture, not a clear solution.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful for comparing suspensions and solutions.

experiments.title: Flour in water review
experiments.focus: Show that some powders create cloudy mixtures instead of clear solutions.
student_observations: The liquid can look cloudy or thick.
The powder does not disappear completely.
Mixtures can have different textures.
experiments.teacher_note: A simple link between physical properties and mixtures.

experiments.title: Gelatin texture review
experiments.focus: Introduce how some mixtures become thicker or more structured.
student_observations: The mixture can become thicker.
Texture can be a clue about the mixture type.
Different materials change physical properties differently.
experiments.teacher_note: Good for a discussion about everyday materials.

experiments.title: Oatmeal mixture review
experiments.focus: Show how a familiar food material behaves when mixed with water.
student_observations: The mixture is not clear.
Some particles may remain visible.
Everyday materials can be mixtures.
experiments.teacher_note: A friendly classroom example for introducing suspensions.

experiments.title: Vinegar and bicarbonate concept
experiments.focus: Introduce a safe, classroom-level acid-carbonate concept with visible gas formation in the model.
student_observations: Bubbles can appear in the model.
Gas may be produced.
This is a useful example of a reaction concept.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep the explanation conceptual and tied to the reaction registry.

experiments.title: Chalk in water mixture
experiments.focus: Show that some solids remain suspended or visible in water.
student_observations: The water can become cloudy.
Solid particles may stay visible.
Not every powder dissolves well.
experiments.teacher_note: Use this as a comparison with sugar dissolving.

experiments.title: Milk and water mixture
experiments.focus: Discuss how everyday liquids can form mixtures with changing appearance.
student_observations: The liquid may look different after mixing.
Everyday liquids can be described as mixtures.
Appearance does not always mean a new substance.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep it simple and observational.

experiments.title: Crystallization review 2
experiments.focus: Review how a dissolved substance can reappear when the solvent is removed.
student_observations: A clear solution can return to a solid form.
Crystals can form from the same substance.
Evaporation and crystallization are linked ideas.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful after solutions and separation lessons.

experiments.title: Solution vs suspension review
experiments.focus: Compare a clear solution with cloudy mixtures and visible particles.
student_observations: Some materials make clear solutions.
Some materials stay visible.
Mixture type depends on the particles and the solvent.
experiments.teacher_note: A good summary activity for revision.

experiments.title: Precipitation concept review
experiments.focus: Introduce the idea that mixing two clear solutions can form a new solid in the model.
student_observations: A new solid can appear in the model.
Not all mixtures stay clear.
Some reactions can produce a precipitate.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep it tied to the validated reaction registry.

experiments.title: Surface tension review
experiments.focus: Review how small amounts of soap can change the behavior of water surfaces.
student_observations: The water surface behaves differently after soap is added.
Bubbles may form more easily.
Physical properties can change without a new substance being created.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful as a quick recap on physical properties.

experiments.title: Acid carbonate review
experiments.focus: Review the acid-carbonate idea as a classroom model that can show gas formation.
student_observations: Gas can be represented in the model.
Bubbles are a useful visual clue.
This helps with reaction classification.
experiments.teacher_note: Use the registry-backed concept rather than a real-lab procedure.

experiments.title: Dissolution comparison review
experiments.focus: Compare several solids that can dissolve in the classroom model.
student_observations: Different solids can dissolve at different rates or in different ways.
Solubility is a useful property.
A clear solution still contains dissolved पदार्थ.
experiments.teacher_note: Helpful for revision and comparison tables.

experiments.title: Mixture classification review
experiments.focus: Group common classroom materials by solution, suspension or immiscible liquid examples.
student_observations: Some mixtures stay clear.
Some mixtures remain cloudy or separate.
Classification depends on how the materials behave together.
experiments.teacher_note: This is a broad summary activity for the whole unit.

experiments.title: Evaporation separation review
experiments.focus: Review how removing water can help separate a dissolved solid from a solution.
student_observations: Liquid can be removed while the solid remains.
Separation methods depend on the mixture type.
Evaporation and crystallization are connected ideas.
experiments.teacher_note: A useful end-of-unit recap.
